output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mostly a result of the late-July night-shift cut, not Haverlow's product. Night receiving went from six to four people. Median time from unload to chamber rose from about 44 minutes to nearly 4 hours. Pallets sit on an unrefrigerated dock averaging 15–17°C. Trailer telematics show Haverlow loads arriving at 2.4–3.5°C, with no alarms. The warm receipt probes were keyed at the end of the long unload, after the product had warmed. Night-shift write-off rates rose to about 2.9% for every supplier, while day-shift rates stayed flat. Chambers held temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or shift volume; the evidence contradicts it. Restore the night team, or otherwise cut the dock dwell, and set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly from scan data. Also move chilled pallets into the chambers first. Keep the receiving probe. Part of the rise in customer credits, which are a smaller share, may come from Corriebank's looser claim rules from 3 August. That is unproven, so request a claim-level extract and reconcile a sample before changing the credit terms. I'm fairly confident in the main diagnosis. The customer-credit part is uncertain.
